ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r7.claim: After exposing idol worship, God confronts them with undeniable evidence: provision, hearing and sight, life and death, and governance of all things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r7.anchor: لما بين فضائح عبدة الأوثان، أتبعها بذكر الدلائل على فساد مذهبهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r8.claim: Provision essential to life comes from rain in the sky and vegetation on earth; min marks its source and indicates generosity from both upper and lower worlds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r8.anchor: فمن السماء بالمطر، ومن الأرض بالنبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r9.claim: Hearing and sight are the two noblest senses: hearing enables perception, sight surveys creation, and God controls their preservation or removal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر ملكه لهاتين الحاستين الشريفتين: السمع الذي هو سبب مدارك الأشياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains God’s control as creating the senses in their remarkable form or protecting them from pervasive injury; Abū Ḥayyān says these nuances do not follow from the wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: من يملك السمع والأبصار من يستطيع خلقهما وتسويتهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r1.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r1.claim: ʿAlī praises God as one who gives sight through fat, hearing through bone, and speech through flesh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r1.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله وجهه: سبحان من بصر بشحم، وأسمع بعظم، وأنطق بلحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r2.claim: Here am signals transition to another proof rather than abrogating the prior question with bal; it cannot be treated as bal without the interrogative hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r2.anchor: وأم هنا تقتضي تقدير بل دون همزة الاستفهام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r3.claim: Hearing and sight stand for the senses generally because they are most distinguished; creating living from dead and dead from living displays God’s power to bring opposites from one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r3.anchor: ونبه تعالى بالسمع والبصر على الحواس لأنهما أشرفها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r4.claim: The universal statement that God governs all things follows four examples because His governance has no limit; the unbelievers cannot deny that God provides, controls, creates life and death, and governs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r4.anchor: ومن يدبر الأمر شامل لما تقدم من الأشياء الأربعة المذكورة ولغيرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r5.claim: “Will you not be mindful?” warns them to fear punishment for inventing partners for God; alternatively it asks them to take warning and stop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r5.anchor: ومعنى أفلا تتقون: أفلا تخافون عقوبة الله في افترائكم

STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r13.claim: False gods will disown their worshippers and cannot create or guide; God alone provides for creatures.
STUDYQURAN:10:intro/r13.anchor: the false gods will reject those who used to serve them (vv.28–29), especially because these false gods have no ability to create or guide others (vv. 34–35). Rather, God is the only One Who can provide for His creatures (v. 31).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: If the Quraysh recognize God as creator, sustainer, and giver of life and death, they should recognize Him alone as Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they should also regard him to be their lord.

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r1.claim: As God alone creates, He alone provides sustenance.

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r2.claim: Bodily provision is obedience granted to some and failures granted to others; spiritual provision is connection for some, heedlessness and later punishment or respite for others.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r2.anchor: وهو لقوم توفيق الطاعات ، ولآخرين خذلان الزلات

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r3.claim: For the spirits, provision means realities of intimacy for some, but worldly heedlessness and eventual punishment or respite for others.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r3.anchor: وللأرواح رزق : وهو لقوم حقائق الوصلة ، ولآخرين - في الدنيا - الغفلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r4.claim: God’s control of hearing and sight means He perfects some people’s vision through monotheism and blinds others to realization.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r4.anchor: فيكمل بعض الأبصار بالتوحيد ، وبعضها يعميها عن التحقيق

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r5.claim: Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living means bringing a believer from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a believer.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r5.anchor: يخرج المؤمن من الكافر ، والكافر من المؤمن

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r6.claim: Although they answer God, they speak from conjecture and words without inward conviction.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r6.anchor: لا عن بصيرة ، ونطقا . . لا عن تصديق سريرة

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r7.claim: All created things and events are subject to divine will, decree, and power; the decree has already passed and cannot be altered.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r7.anchor: سبق لهم الحكم ، وصدق فيهم القول ؛ فلا لحكمه تحويل ولا لقوله تبديل

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r8.claim: Causes cannot alter what is eternal or reverse God’s decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r8.anchor: فلا لحكمه تحويل ولا لقوله تبديل ، فإن العلل لا تغير الأزل

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r9.claim: He rejects both assigning partners in creation under the doctrine of predestination and denying God’s power to resurrect; both are unbelief.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r9.anchor: قوم جعلوا له في الإيجاد شركاء بدعوى القدر ، وقوم منعوا جواز قدرته على الإعادة

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r10.claim: Truth is a divine name: God exists, possesses truth, and makes truth actual; for creatures, truth is good action, sound belief, and permissible speech.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r10.anchor: الحق اسم من أسمائه سبحانه ، ومعناه أنه موجود ، وأنه ذو الحق

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r12.claim: Conjecture favors one judgment without certainty; it is defective regarding God, while certainty about one’s own future is also defective.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r12.anchor: فالظن في أوصاف الحق معلول ، والقطع - في أوصاف النفس - لكل أحد معلول

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r13.claim: A servant should not presume to know his own unseen future, but should have certainty about God; the Prophet and his followers are told to call with insight.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r13.anchor: والعبد يجب أن يكون في الحال خاليا عن الظن إذ لا يعرف أحد غيب نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r14.claim: The heedless grow blinder the more they hear the Qur’an, while people of spiritual realization grow in guidance; God’s address confuses some and enlightens others.
QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r14.anchor: انسدت بصائرهم فلا يزدادون بكثرة سماع القرآن إلا عمى على عمى

SULAMI:v1p301#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p301#3/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p301#3/r1.claim: The question about God's management of affairs points to the changing turns of the cosmos.

SULAMI:v1p301#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p301#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p301#3/r2.claim: God initiates and renews affairs through time and manages them; this leaves no basis for claiming independent agency through one's own acts and work.
SULAMI:v1p301#3/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : من يبدئ أمره ويعيده ، ويبديه في أوقاته السائرة

AKHFASH:v1p373/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p373/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p373/r4.claim: أم can precede من because من is not inherently interrogative but stands in place of the interrogative alif; أم supplies an indispensable meaning.
AKHFASH:v1p373/r4.anchor: وقال {أمن يملك السمع والأبصار} فان قلت "كيف دخلت (أم) على (من) فلأن (من) ليست في الاصل للاستفهام وانما يستغنى بها عن الالف

AKHFASH:v1p373/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p373/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p373/r5.claim: The same explanation allows an interrogative particle to precede هل; interrogation originally belongs to the alif.
AKHFASH:v1p373/r5.anchor: فلذلك أدخلت عليها (أم) كما ادخلت على (هل) حرف الاستفهام وانما الاستفهام في الاصل الالف. و (أم) تدخل لمعنى لا بد منه.

AKHFASH:v1p373/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p373/r6.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p373/r6.claim: A poem's هل ... أم هل construction illustrates أم following هل.
AKHFASH:v1p373/r6.anchor: أبا مالك هل لمتني مذ حضضتني * على القتل أم هل لامني لك لائم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r1.claim: God alone decides and carries out the affair.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد يدبر الامر قال : يقضيه وحده

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r2.claim: Fearing God means guarding against Hell through the five daily prayers.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : افلا تتقون قال : تتقون النار بالصلوات الخمس .

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r3.claim: An alternative gloss reads the question as asking whether they are able to fear God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r1.claim: Provision from heaven is rain, and provision from earth is all vegetation, including grain, fruit, and pasture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r1.anchor: فالرزق من السماء المطر ، والرزق من الأرض النبات كله من حب وثمر وكلأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r2.claim: Am marks a transition to another question; God's ownership of hearing and sight means control over their creation, recalling the useful and subtle creation of these faculties.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى : { يملك السمع والأبصار } يملك التصرف فيهما ، وهو ملك إيجاد تينك الحاستين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r3.claim: Hearing is a singular verbal noun that denotes the species collectively; sight is plural to make universal intent explicit and avoid a possible reference to one particular sight, unlike the individual faculties addressed in 17:36.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r3.anchor: وأفرد { السمع } لأنه مصدر فهو دال على الجنس الموجود في جميع حواس الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r4.claim: Life emerging from death includes animal offspring from initially lifeless sperm or eggs as they develop; death emerging from life means sperm or eggs produced by animals. The definite terms mean the species.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r4.anchor: هو تولد أطفال الحيوان من النطف ومن البيض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r5.claim: The reciprocal creation is phrased as a riddle with antithesis to heighten wonder; unlike the similar passage in 3:27, this one carries no allusion to anything hidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r5.anchor: وقد نظم هذا الاستدلال على ذلك الصنع العجيب بأسلوب الأحاجي والألغاز وجعل بمحسن التضاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r6.claim: The question who directs affairs generalizes after the specific signs in human beings, like the appeal to observe oneself and the heavens in 51:21–22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p155#2/r6.anchor: وهو هنا تعميم بعد تخصيص ذكر ما فيه مزيد عبرة في أنفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r1.claim: The first fa treats the Prophet's command to ask as a condition: if he asks who provides and creates, the polytheists will say God; compare the same construction at 17:51–52.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r1.anchor: فنزل فعل { قل } منزلة الشرط فكأنه قيل : إن تقل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض فسيقولون الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r2.claim: Some grammarians explain command constructions with a supplied conditional; the author says this is close to the more semantic analysis that treats the command itself as a condition, differing mainly in whether the estimate is grammatical or interpretive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r2.anchor: والرأيان متقاربان إلا أن ما سلكه المحققون تقدير معنى والتقدير عندهم اعتبار لا استعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r3.claim: Without treating the command as a condition, the fa would not appear, as in the distinct question-and-answer construction at 23:84–85.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r3.anchor: ولو لم ينزل الأمر بمنزلة الشرط لما جاءت الفاء كما في قوله تعالى : { قل لمن الأرض ومن فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r4.claim: The fa in then say is explanatory: if they answer, ask whether they will not fear God by rejecting partners; the fa in the final question draws that rebuke from their admission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r4.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فقل } فاء الفصيحة ، أي إن قالوا ذلك فقل أفلا تتقون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r5.claim: The object of fear is omitted but understood as God; the polytheists already acknowledged God alone as provider, creator, and director in many Quranic passages, and their inability to deny this truth leaves them convicted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p156/r5.anchor: وإنما أخبر الله عنهم بأنهم سيعترفون بأن الرازق والخالق والمدبر هو الله لأنهم لم يكونوا يعتقدون غير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r1.claim: The questions are a rebuke and proof with no escape: God provides rain from heaven and growth from earth, owns hearing and sight, brings life from death and death from life, and governs all affairs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r1.anchor: هذا توقيف وتوبيخ واحتجاج لا محيد عن التزامه، ومن السماء يريد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.claim: Examples of bringing the living from the dead include an embryo from semen, bird from egg, and growing plant from earth; the reverse includes egg from bird, while divine governance proceeds through complete, eternal knowledge rather than thought or change.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.anchor: ويخرج الحي من الميت الجنين من النطفة، والطائر من البيضة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.claim: They have no answer but God; once they admit His power, the rebuke asks why they do not fear Him instead of treating idols as gods.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.anchor: فسيقولون الله لا مندوحة لهم عن ذلك، ولا تمكنهم المباهتة بسواه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r1.claim: God provides rain from heaven and plants from earth; He created hearing and sight and brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, as previously discussed at 3:27.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r1.anchor: المطر ومن الأرض النبات ( أم من يملك السمع ) أي خلق السمع والأبصار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r2.claim: God directs the affairs of this world and the next; the audience admits it is God because only He can do these things, proving His oneness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ( ومن يدبر الأمر ) أي أمر الدنيا والآخرة ( فسيقولون الله ) لأنهم خوطبوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets “will you not be mindful?” as “will you not take warning?”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r4.claim: Muqatil reads the question as “will you not fear associating partners with God?”

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r1.claim: Rainwater makes crops grow by God's power, as illustrated by the listed produce; the question about who provides it invokes 80:27–31 and 67:21 to establish His exclusive lordship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r1.anchor: من ذا الذي ينزل من السماء ماء المطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r2.claim: God gave people hearing and sight and could take them away; Ibn Kathīr links this to 67:23 and 6:46.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r2.anchor: الذي وهبكم هذه القوة السامعة، والقوة الباصرة، ولو شاء لذهب بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.claim: Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living occurs by God's immense power and grace; the verse is general and includes all the interpretations previously discussed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.anchor: بقدرته العظيمة، ومنته العميمة، وقد تقدم ذكر الخلاف في ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.claim: God alone governs all creation and none can overturn His judgment; every heavenly and earthly creature depends on Him, as in 55:29.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.anchor: وهو المتصرف الحاكم الذي لا معقب لحكمه، ولا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.claim: Since the polytheists admit God does all this, they should fear Him instead of worshiping others through opinion and ignorance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.anchor: أفلا تخافون منه أن تعبدوا معه غيره

JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.claim: God brings worshippers together with idols, then separates the parties, who disavow one another; idols are also brought to life.
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.anchor: وتدل على أنه يجمع بين من عبد غيره وبين معبوده

JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.claim: Everyone receives the consequence of good or evil; no manufactured deity can help, harm, avert punishment, or independently intercede with God.
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن كل أحد ينال جزاء ما قدم من خير أو شر

JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.claim: Worshipping idols and fabricating claims are human acts, for which people are punished and reproached, against the Compulsionists' account of human acts.
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة والافتراء فعلهم؛ لذلك عاقبهم ووبخهم به

JISHUMI:v5p3361/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r5.claim: Rizq is an ongoing gift or benefit its recipient may use and others may not withhold; only God is called the Provider because He creates provision, like the exclusive title Lord despite ordinary possessive uses.
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r5.anchor: الرزق في اللغة: هو العطاء الجاري، ومنه: رزق السلطان

JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.claim: The questions establish God's unity and resurrection: God sends rain and produces plants, or sends clouds, rain, celestial bodies, and vegetation, as al-Aṣamm explains.
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.anchor: ثم قرر تعالى عليهم أدلة التوحيد والبعث

JISHUMI:v5p3362/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r2.claim: God owns hearing and sight by creating and arranging these faculties, granting or taking them away, or enabling people to hear admonition and see lessons.
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r2.anchor: وقيل: من يملك السمع فيسمعها المواعظ، والأبصار فيريها العظات

JISHUMI:v5p3362/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r3.claim: Bringing the living from the dead may mean a human from a drop and a drop from a human, or giving and taking life; God's management includes day and night, seasons, people, life, and death.
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r3.anchor: قيل: النطفة من الإنسان والإنسان من النطفة، وقيل: من يحييكم إذا كنتم أحياء

JISHUMI:v5p3362/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r4.claim: The polytheists will acknowledge that God performs these acts, so they should fear His punishment and worship no other.
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r4.anchor: فسيقولون الله يعني: هو الله تعالى يفعل هذه الأشياء، فقل لهم أفلا تتقون عقابه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r1.claim: God provides from heaven and earth, pouring out His favors and widening His mercy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r1.anchor: أي يرزقكم منهما جميعا ، لم يقتصر برزقكم على جهة واحدة ليفيض عليكم نعمته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r2.claim: ‘Who owns hearing and sight?’ asks who creates and fashions them remarkably, or who protects these delicate organs from many hazards.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r2.anchor: من يستطيع خلقهما وتسويتهما على الحد الذي سويا عليه من الفطرة العجيبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r3.claim: Managing affairs means directing the whole world, stated generally after specific examples.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r3.anchor: ومن يلي تدبير أمر العالم كله ، جاء بالعموم بعد الخصوص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r4.claim: ‘Will you not fear?’ means protect yourselves from punishment for your misguidance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r4.anchor: أفلا تقون أنفسكم ولا تحذرون عليها عقابه فيما أنتم بصدده من الضلال

MUQATIL:10:31-35/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:31-35/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:31-35/r1.claim: Rain and crops, hearing and sight, life from semen and death from the living, and governance belong to God; Quraysh acknowledge this, so they should abandon shirk and fear punishment.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r1.claim: God provides from heaven through rain and from earth through vegetation.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ قل من يرزقكم من السماء ﴾ بالمطر ﴿ والأرض ﴾ بالنبات

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r2.claim: God alone creates and forms hearing and sight in their astonishing detail, or protects their delicate organs from injury over time.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r2.anchor: من يستطيع خلقهما وتسويتهما على الحد الذى سويا عليه من القطرة العجيبة أو من يحميها من الآفات

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r3.claim: Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living can mean animals, chicks, crops, believers, and scholars from fluids, eggs, and seeds, and their opposites.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r3.anchor: أي الحيوان والفرخ والزرع والمؤمن والعالم من النطفة والبيضة والحب والكافر والجاهل وعكسها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r4.claim: Management of the whole world follows the particular examples, widening the argument from specific divine powers to universal governance.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ ومن يدبر الأمر ﴾ ومن يلى تدبير أمر العالم كله جاء بالعموم بعد الخصوص

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r5.claim: Since they acknowledge God as the only one able to do these things, they should abandon associating partners with Him in worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r5.anchor: ﴿ فسيقولون الله ﴾ فسيجيبونك عند سؤالك أن القادر على هذه هو الله ﴿ فقل أفلا تتقون ﴾

QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r1.claim: The passage rebuts polytheists and establishes the proof: if they acknowledge God's acts, the case is clear; if not, any rational person must recognize that the heavens and earth have a creator, a truth close to immediate necessity.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r1.anchor: المراد بمساق هذا الكلام الرد على المشركين وتقرير الحجة عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r2.claim: Provision from heaven is rain and provision from earth is vegetation.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r3.claim: God owns hearing and sight because He made and created them for people.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r3.anchor: { أمن يملك السمع والأبصار } أي من جعلهما

QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r4.claim: Examples of bringing the living from the dead include vegetation from earth, a person from a sperm drop, an ear of grain from a seed, a bird from an egg, and a believer from a disbeliever.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r4.anchor: { ومن يخرج الحي من الميت } أي النبات من الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r5.claim: Managing the affair means determining and carrying it out.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r5.anchor: { ومن يدبر الأمر } أي يقدره ويقضيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r6.claim: The polytheists will answer “God,” since they believe He is the Creator; alternatively, an honest and thoughtful person will reach this answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r6.anchor: { فسيقولون الله } لأنهم كانوا يعتقدون أن الخالق هو الله

QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r7.claim: The concluding question urges them to fear God's punishment and retribution in this life and the next.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r7.anchor: أفلا تخافون عقابه ونقمته في الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r1.claim: After exposing idol worship, the author argues from provision, senses, life and death, and God's governance against associating partners with Him.
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r1.anchor: لما بين فضائح عبدة الأوثان أتبعها بذكر الدلائل الدالة على فساد هذا المذهب

RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r2.claim: Provision depends on rain from the sky and nourishment from the earth; plants originate in earth and animal diets must ultimately reach plants, since an endless chain of animals eating animals is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r2.anchor: ولا يمكن أن يكون غذاء كل حيوان حيوانا آخر وإلا لزم الذهاب إلى ما لا نهاية له وذلك محال

RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r3.claim: Since only God governs the heavens and earth, He alone provides; hearing and sight are the noblest senses.
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r3.anchor: فلزم القطع بأن الأرزاق لا تحصل إلا من السماء والأرض ، ومعلوم أن مدبر السموات والأرضين ليس إلا الله سبحانه وتعالى

RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r4.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī is quoted praising the Creator who gives sight through fat, hearing through bone, and speech through flesh.
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r4.anchor: وكان علي رضي الله عنه يقول : سبحان من بصر بشحم ، وأسمع بعظم ، وأنطق بلحم

RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r5.claim: The living from the dead and dead from the living may mean humans and birds from sperm and eggs and vice versa, or believers from unbelievers and vice versa; most favor the first, closer to the literal sense.
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r5.anchor: والأكثرون على القول الأول ، وهو إلى الحقيقة أقرب

RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r6.claim: The general statement that God directs affairs summarizes limitless governance in the upper and lower worlds and in the worlds of spirits and bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r6.anchor: أقسام تدبير الله تعالى في العالم العلوي وفي العالم السفلي وفي عالمي الأرواح والأجساد أمور لا نهاية لها

RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r7.claim: The Meccan polytheists acknowledged God as provider and governor but claimed idols brought them near or interceded, despite knowing idols neither benefit nor harm; they should fear assigning them worship.
RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r7.anchor: فعند ذلك قال لرسوله عليه السلام : { فقل أفلا تتقون } يعني أفلا تتقون أن تجعلوا هذه الأوثان شركاء لله في المعبودية

SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r1.claim: من السماء may mark origin, part, or kind; the partitive and kind readings require an omitted أهل.
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r1.anchor: من " يجوز أن تكون لابتداء الغاية، وأن تكون للتبعيض، وأن تكون لبيان الجنس

SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r2.claim: أم is disconnected because no interrogative hamza or equivalence preceded it; here it means بل alone since an explicit interrogative من follows.
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r2.anchor: هذه " أم " المنقطعة لأنه لم تتقدمها همزة استفهام ولا تسوية، ولكن إنما تقدر هنا ب " بل " وحدها

SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r3.claim: The transition is a transfer to a new point, not cancellation of what came before, following the Qur'anic pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r3.anchor: والإضراب هنا على القاعدة المقررة في القرآن أنه إضراب انتقال لا إضراب إبطال

STUDYQURAN:10:31/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r1.speaker: Bg, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r1.claim: Provision from Heaven and earth refers respectively to rain and vegetation.
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r1.anchor: From the Heaven and earth is understood to be a reference to rain and vegetation, respectively (Bg, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:10:31/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r2.claim: Other commentators understand provision from Heaven and earth to include both bodily and spiritual sustenance.
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r2.anchor: such provision can be both bodily and spiritual (Q)

STUDYQURAN:10:31/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r3.speaker: Bg, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r3.claim: Having power over hearing and sight means giving people hearing and sight.
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r3.anchor: “Who gives you hearing and sight?” (Bg, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:10:31/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r4.claim: The question about bringing the living from the dead and dead from the living is answered in 30:19 and related passages.
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r4.anchor: A response to the question, Who brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living? can be seen in 30:19

STUDYQURAN:10:31/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r5.claim: The respondents are the Makkans, who answer “God” because His agency comes immediately to mind, especially as many viewed Allah as head of an Arab pantheon.
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r5.anchor: they, namely, the Makkans (R), will say, “God”

STUDYQURAN:10:31/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r6.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r6.claim: The call to reverence targets the Makkans' association of idols with God and warns them of their error and its coming punishment.
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r6.anchor: addresses the Makkans’ seeing idols as partners with God and is meant to alert them to their current state of error and the impending punishment

STUDYQURAN:10:31/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r7.claim: God's directing the affair is discussed at 10:3.
STUDYQURAN:10:31/r7.anchor: For God’s directing the affair, see 10:3c

TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r1.claim: God controls hearing and sight, can strengthen or take them away, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and governs all affairs; the audience admits He does this, so they are asked why they do not fear His punishment and abandon shirk.
TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r1.anchor: {أمن يملك السمع والأبصار} [يونس: 31] يقول: أم من ذا الذي يملك أسماعكم وأبصاركم التي تسمعون بها أن يزيد في قواها

TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r2.claim: God governs the affairs of the heavens, earth, all within them, and human beings; the people answer that God does all this.
TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r2.anchor: من يدبر أمر السماء والأرض وما فيهن وأمركم وأمر الخلق.

ZAJJAJ:v3p16#2/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p16#2/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p16#2/r9.claim: The questions about provision, hearing, sight, life, death, and governance establish God’s oneness because only God can do these things; the audience answers ‘God.’
ZAJJAJ:v3p16#2/r9.anchor:
لما خوطبوا بما لا يقدر عليه إلا الله - جل وعز - كان فيه دليل على
توحيده.

TABATABAI:10:31/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31/r1.claim: The verse sets out three ordered proofs of divine lordship: one addressed through the idolaters’ own account of cosmic management, one through afterlife accountability, and one through the truth sought by spiritual elect.
TABATABAI:10:31/r1.anchor: وهي ثلاث حجج مرتبة بحسب الدقة والمتانة

TABATABAI:10:31/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31/r2.claim: The first proof meets idolaters on their premise that distinct deities manage different domains and are worshiped to secure benefits or avert harm.
TABATABAI:10:31/r2.anchor: فإنهم إنما يعبدون أرباب الأصنام بأصنامهم من جهة تدبيرهم للكون

TABATABAI:10:31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31/r3.claim: Since God alone ultimately manages humans and all other beings, He alone deserves worship and lordship.
TABATABAI:10:31/r3.anchor: تدبير العالم الإنساني وسائر الموجودات جميعا يقوم به الله سبحانه لا غير

TABATABAI:10:31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31/r4.claim: The order of the arguments is deliberate; without this distinction, the author says one might expect the proofs about the afterlife and truth to precede the proof engaging idolaters.
TABATABAI:10:31/r4.anchor: ولولا اعتبار هذه النكتة كان الظاهر أن تذكر أولا الحجة الثانية ثم الثالثة ثم الأولى

TABATABAI:10:31#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r1.claim: Life first appears to mean the principle enabling knowledge and power; inquiry extends it from animals to plants, whose vital processes disclose life too.
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r1.anchor: ثم اكتشف من طريق النظر العلمي أن ذلك لا يختص بأقسام الحيوان

TABATABAI:10:31#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r2.claim: More broadly, life is the capacity to yield fitting effects and death their absence; the definition applies to earth, actions, words, and the human being.
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r2.anchor: ثم الحياة وهي تقابل الموت الذي هو بطلان مبدأ الأعمال الحيوية تعود بحسب التحليل

TABATABAI:10:31#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r3.claim: The Qur’an calls religion life because true Islam is the divinely created human nature.
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r3.anchor: ولذا عد القرآن الشريف الدين حياة للإنسان لأنه يرى أن الدين الحق وهو الإسلام هو الفطرة الإلهية

TABATABAI:10:31#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r4.claim: On narrower definitions, the expression means an animal, or an animal or plant, coming from nonliving matter and nonliving parts separating from living organisms.
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r4.anchor: فعلى النظرتين الأوليين هو خروج الحيوان أو الحيوان والنبات بالكينونة من غيرها

TABATABAI:10:31#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r5.claim: The verse’s context favors the broad functional sense: something beneficial or alive emerges from an unproductive or dead source, and the reverse occurs.
TABATABAI:10:31#2/r5.anchor: وظاهر الآية الكريمة بالنظر إلى سياقها ومقام المخاطبة فيها أن يكون المراد

TABATABAI:10:31-32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r1.claim: The verse counters the idolaters’ argument for separate managing gods by showing that all management, both human-specific and universal, ends with God.
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r1.anchor: والآية ترد عليهم حجتهم ببيان انتهاء التدبيرات المختلفة إليه تعالى

TABATABAI:10:31-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r2.claim: Because the questions progress from human sustenance to hearing, sight, and life, “bringing living from dead” here likely means bringing a human life of reason and religion from its opposite.
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r2.anchor: فالمراد بإخراج الحي من الميت وبالعكس - والله أعلم - إخراج الإنسان الحي بالسعادة الإنسانية

TABATABAI:10:31-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r3.claim: Rain, plant growth, and sensory powers sustain and let people use provision; without hearing and sight, people would fail to benefit and perish.
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r3.anchor: { أمن يملك السمع والأبصار } منكم فتتم بهما فائدة رزقكم

TABATABAI:10:31-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r4.claim: The final question about who manages all affairs makes the proof universal; the polytheists answer “God,” since they acknowledge His ultimate management.
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r4.anchor: فسيقولون الله } اعترافا بأنه الذي ينتهي إليه جميع هذه التدبيرات في الإنسان وغيره

TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.claim: The admission entails that God is the true Lord and deserves exclusive worship; if truth and guidance are with Him, worship of other supposed lords is error.
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.anchor: فإن الهدى مع الحق لا غير فلا يبقى عند غيره الذي هو الباطل إلا الضلال

ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n49/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n49/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n49/r1.claim: Rizq means both physical and spiritual sustenance, accounting for references to heaven and earth as well as hearing and sight.
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n49/r1.anchor: used here in both the physical and spiritual connotations of this word

ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r1.claim: The addressed polytheists believe God exists but also assign divine or semi-divine qualities to beings they worship as intermediaries to approach Him.
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r1.anchor: there are beings endowed with certain divine or semi-divine qualities, thus having, as it were, a "share" in God's divinity

ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r2.claim: This belief violates God’s oneness and uniqueness, depriving their belief in God of its true meaning and spiritual value.
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n50/r2.anchor: it deprives those people's belief in God of its true meaning and spiritual value

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r1.claim: The one who provides from sky and earth sends rain and brings out plants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r1.anchor: القطر من السماء ويخرج النبات من الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r2.claim: Owning hearing and sight means creating them for people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r3.claim: Bringing the living from the dead includes believer from disbeliever, plant from earth, human from sperm, bird from egg, stalk from grain, and palm from seed, with the reverse process likewise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r3.anchor: أي المؤمن من الكافر، والنبات من الأرض، والإنسان من النطفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r4.claim: God directs the affairs of this world and the next; the audience admits He does these things, so they are challenged to fear Him and abandon partners.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r2.claim: God sends rain and grows plants, created hearing and sight, and brings believers from disbelievers, plants from earth, and people from semen, as well as their opposites.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r3.claim: God directs the affairs of this world and the next; since people admit He does these things, they should fear Him and associate nothing with Him.

ELMALILI:10:31/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r1.claim: God supplies provisions from heaven and earth and owns, creates, equips, governs, and controls hearing and sight, the most noble faculties and means of using provision.
ELMALILI:10:31/r1.anchor: Yani o rızıklarla intifâ‘ın en mühim vesâit ve şerâitinden olan his kuvvelerinin en şereflisi bulunan işitme ve görme melekeleri gibi nimeti kim veriyor?

ELMALILI:10:31/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r2.claim: The singular 'hearing' and plural 'sights' suggest that seeing is more various or numerous than hearing.
ELMALILI:10:31/r2.anchor: müfred, “ebsâr”ın cemi‘olarak îrâdı görmenin işitmeden kesretli olduğuna

ELMALILI:10:31/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r3.claim: Ownership of hearing and sight points to the divine source of recognizing truth, the beginning of certainty, and insight into external reality.

ELMALILI:10:31/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r4.claim: True hearing, seeing, and perceiving truth are directly divine acts; he also connects this to the sacred hadith on God becoming the servant's hearing through supererogatory devotion.
ELMALILI:10:31/r4.anchor: doğru görmek ve doğru işitmek, hak ve hakikati hiss ü idrak etmek işinin

ELMALILI:10:31/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r5.claim: Life comes from lifeless matter and returns to death: living plants, animals, and people appear, and organic life develops from food and inorganic material.
ELMALILI:10:31/r5.anchor: Dün ortada yokken bugün bir zîhayat, bir nebat, bir hayvan, bir insan meydana geliyor ve birtakım hayatsız maddelerden çıkıp geliyor. Ve sonra ölüyor

ELMALILI:10:31/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r6.claim: These transformations between opposed natures violate sameness and regularity, so they indicate an active power beyond nature that makes causes and effects change places.
ELMALILI:10:31/r6.anchor: tabiatın kānûn-ı esâsîsi olan ıttırad ve ayniyete muhalif ve binâen‘aleyh hilâf-ı tabiat hâdisâttır

ELMALILI:10:31/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r7.claim: God manages the whole universe's affairs and order by command, not only the acts of creating the particular phenomena named.
ELMALILI:10:31/r7.anchor: Yani yalnız o zikrolunan husûsât değil, daha bunlar gibi nice ezdâd ve tabâyi‘-i muhtelife ile meşhun olan ale’lumûm âlemin şuûn ve umûrunu tedbir ve idare eden

ELMALILI:10:31/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:31/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:31/r8.claim: Even polytheists readily answer that God does these things when they reflect; the closing question challenges them to fear His power and avoid associating partners and disobeying Him.
ELMALILI:10:31/r8.anchor: Bu suâllerin cevâbı gayet vâzıh olduğundan müşrikler bile bunları teemmül edince hep bunları Allah yapıyor demekte tereddüt göstermeyeceklerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r1.claim: Sustenance is especially important because all other resources matter only while life continues; it depends on both heavenly conditions such as rain, sunlight, and warmth and earthly resources and habitats, all graciously provided by God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r1.anchor: Hayatı devam ettiren rızıkların hem semavî hem de yere (arz) ait şartlarla ilişkisi vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r2.claim: These provisions would be useless unless God also equipped people to benefit from them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r2.anchor: Allah insan oğluna gerek semavî gerekse yere ait imkânlardan yararlanmak için lüzumlu olan donanımı sağlamasaydı bu nimetlerin hiçbir anlamı olmazdı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r3.claim: God’s control of hearing and sight means these key senses operate under His laws so people can benefit from the provision He sends from heaven and earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r3.anchor: işitme ve görme duyularının, Allah’ın yasaları altında, O’nun gökten ve yerden verdiği rızıklardan istifade edecek şekilde işlemesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r4.speaker: Hz. Ali
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r4.claim: Ali marvels at the power that enables sight through a fluid, hearing through a bone, and speech through a piece of flesh.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r4.anchor: Hz. Ali’nin, “Bir sıvı”yla (göz bebeği) görmemizi, bir kemikle (kulak kemiği) işitmemizi, bir et parçasıyla (dil) konuşmamızı sağlayan kudret

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r5.claim: God brings living beings from lifeless things and makes the living lifeless; He rules heaven, earth, humanity, life, and every affair.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:31/r5.anchor: Cansız nesnelerden canlıları yaratan da canlıları cansız haline getiren de O’dur

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Arabs acknowledged God as creator, master, and governor, but treated their deities as favored creatures and intercessors; these beliefs undermine both denial of resurrection and associating partners with God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: They were able to convince God to do what they wanted. So, if they could be made happy, they could intercede for them before God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: If the Arabs acknowledged God's sole creative power and governance, they should fear attributing false things to Him and denying His attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: if they have all these beliefs, do they not fear the wrath of God since they attribute baseless things to Him and negate all His high attributes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Arabs considered God creator, sustainer, giver of human reason, life and death, and governor; Islahi agrees, explaining their deities as supposed favorites delegated God's prerogatives, including sustenance and children.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: In my opinion, this view is correct. The Arabs never regarded their deities to be those who administered the universe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Modern idolaters do not differ substantially from the Arabs: both forms of polytheism are the same, despite modern efforts to label their practices monotheistic.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The fact is that both are the same.

QIRAAT-ER:10:31:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:10:31:18#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:10:31:18#1/r1.claim: The lighter mayt reading drops yāʾ gemination; some grammarians distinguish mayt as already dead from mayyit as dying or recently dead.
QIRAAT-ER:10:31:18#1/r1.anchor: Vowel reduction: mayyiti → mayti — dropping the shaddah (gemination) on yāʾ

QIRAAT-ER:10:31:21#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:10:31:21#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:10:31:21#1/r1.claim: This is the same reduction in the accusative form: mayyita becomes mayta by dropping yāʾ gemination.
QIRAAT-ER:10:31:21#1/r1.anchor: Same vowel-reduction variant as word 18 — mayyita → mayta, dropping gemination on yāʾ

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r1.claim: The questions challenge the polytheists to acknowledge God's exclusive right to divinity. Provision comes from heavenly causes such as rain and sun and earthly materials; the earth receives what the sky provides.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r1.anchor: احتجاجا على حقية التوحيد وبطلان ماهم عليه من الإشراك

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r2.claim: For من السماء والأرض, من may mark origin; alternatives take it as explanatory after an ellipsis or partitive after an implied إضافة, meaning provisions from the inhabitants of heaven and earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r2.anchor: فمن على هذا لإبتداء الغاية وقيل : هي لبيان ( من ) على تقدير المضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r3.claim: The disconnected أم introduces a transition, not a correction, and asks who creates and forms hearing and sight, protects them from injury, or controls their persistence and loss; الملك is figurative in these readings.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r3.anchor: ( أم ) منقطعة بمعنى بل والإضطراب إنتقالي لا إبطالي

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r4.claim: The reading of ملك السمع والأبصار as creating them best matches the sequence pairing creative power with provision, as in the cited question about any creator who provides.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r4.anchor: وقيل : والمعنى الأول أوفق لنظم الخالقية مع الرازقية

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r5.claim: The living brought from the dead can mean an animal from a drop and a drop from an animal, or bringing life from death and death from life; interpreting the pair as believer and unbeliever is also reported, while the first explanation is preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r5.anchor: ومن الناس من فسر الحي والميت هنا بالمؤمن والكافر والأول أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r6.claim: Managing the affair generalizes beyond the specific visible matters just listed and signals that all affairs originate with God and return to Him, although humans cannot know their full details.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r6.anchor: وهو تعميم بعد تخصيص ما اندرج تحته من الأمور الظاهرة بالذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r7.claim: The polytheists answer Allah without hesitation because the evidence is too plain for denial; الله is the subject with an omitted predicate meaning that God alone performs these acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r7.anchor: لا مجال للمكابرة والعناد في شيء من ذلك لغاية وضوحه

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r8.claim: The verse does not explicitly call God one of the inhabitants of heaven and earth; although texts say He is in heaven in a manner befitting Him, there is no need to change من from its origin sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r8.anchor: لم يرد صريحا كونه تعالى من أهل السماء والأرض وأن ورد كونه جل وعلا في السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r9.speaker: صاحب الإنتصاف
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r9.claim: He reads the verse as refuting the Qadariyyah claim that God provides only lawful sustenance while people provide themselves with forbidden sustenance, exposing that claim as hidden associationism.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r9.anchor: هذه الآية كافحة لوجوه القدرية الزاعمين أن الأرزاق منقسة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r10.claim: Some mystics claim the cosmic pole manages the world and holds up the sky; they may answer that it acts by God's permission, and use المدبرات أمرا for a non-divine manager.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r10.anchor: يزعمون أن الذي يدبر الأمر في كل عصر قطبه وهو عماد السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r1.claim: Some argue that the pole and God differ only in consideration because the pole has attained perfect nearness; critics say this collapses into unity of being, which most theologians and some Sufis, including al-Imām al-Rabbānī, reject.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r1.anchor: فالقول بأن القطب هو المدبر كالقول بأن الله سبحانه هو المدبر بلافرق

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r2.claim: The proposed analogy between a pole and the angels or Jesus managing by God's permission fails: the question asks for the ultimate source to which management returns, so the polytheists can only answer God.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r2.anchor: وأجيب بأن السؤال إنما هو عمن ينتهي إليه الأمر فلا يتسنى لهم إلا الجواب المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r3.claim: In أفلا تتقون, the interrogative rebukes the actual failure to fear, with the connective following an implied premise: you know this, yet do not fear; the omitted object is God's punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r3.anchor: أي أتعلمون ذلك فلا تتقون والخلاف في مثل هذا التركيب شهير

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r4.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī's analysis appears to make تتقون govern two objects, but al-Ālūsī rejects that implication: here it governs one, with the object omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r4.anchor: وكلام القاضي يوهم أنه متعد إلى مفعولين وليس بذاك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r1.claim: God provides rain from the sky and plants from the earth, grants hearing and sight, brings living things from dead matter and dead matter from living things, and governs events.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض} أي: من السماء بالمطر، ومن الأرض بالنبات،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r2.claim: He brings a living being from a sperm-drop and the sperm-drop from a living being.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r2.anchor: يخرج الحي من النطفة والنطفة من الحي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r3.claim: The Arabs acknowledge that God performs these acts; they are therefore asked why they do not fear His punishment for associating partners with Him, or why they still commit shirk despite that acknowledgment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r3.anchor: {فسيقولون الله} هو الذي يفعل هذه الأشياء، {فقل أفلا تتقون} أفلا تخافون عقابه في شرككم؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r1.claim: Provision from heaven and earth comes from both, from each broadly, or from their inhabitants with an omitted noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r1.anchor: أي منهما جميعا فإن الأرزاق تحصل بأسباب سماوية ومواد أرضية أو { من } كل واحد منهما توسعة عليكم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r2.claim: Owning hearing and sight means creating and shaping them or protecting them from frequent, easily triggered harm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r2.anchor: أم من يستطيع خلقهما وتسويتهما، أو من يحفظهما من الآفات مع كثرتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r3.claim: Bringing living from dead means giving life and death, or creating animals from sperm and sperm from animals.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r3.anchor: ومن يخرج الحى من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحى } ومن يحيي ويميت، أو من ينشىء الحيوان من النطفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r4.claim: Managing the world generalizes after the specific powers; people will answer God because the proof is too clear to deny.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r4.anchor: ومن يدبر الأمر } ومن يلي تدبير أمر العالم وهو تعميم بعد تخصيص. { فسيقولون الله }

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r5.claim: They should fear God's punishment rather than associate partners who share none of His powers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r5.anchor: أنفسكم عقابه بإشراككم إياه ما لا يشاركه في شيء من ذلك.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r5.claim: The questions about provision, senses, life, death, and universal governance expose what the polytheists already admit, thereby proving God’s exclusive divinity and rebuking their denial of resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r5.anchor: فوبخهم بأن وجه السؤال إليهم عما هم معترفون بأنه مختص به ويدل قطعا على تفرده بجميع الأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r6.claim: God provides rain and other benefits from the sky, and plants and other means of life from the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r6.anchor: أي يجلب لكم الخيرات ايها المنكرون للبعث المدعون للشركة { من السمآء } أي بالمطر وغيره من المنافع { والأرض } بالنبات وغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r7.claim: Hearing is singular because most people share it equally, while eyes are plural; sight and hearing sustain bodily life and knowledge sustains spiritual life.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r7.anchor: ووحده للتساوي فيه في الغالب { والأبصار } التي تبصرون بها ما أنعم عليكم به في خلقها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r1.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r1.claim: Ali marvels that God made people see through fat, hear through bone, and speak through flesh.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r1.anchor: قال : سبحانه من بصر بشحم , وأسمع بعظم , وأنطق بلحم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r2.claim: The questioning moves from the obvious gifts people experience to the prior origin of creation: living beings emerge from dead matter and dead matter from living beings.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r2.anchor: نبههم على ما قبله من بدء الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r3.claim: The life/death contrast covers animals and plants as well as a sperm drop and its products, moving from deficiency to completion.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r3.anchor: من الحيوان والنبات { من الميت } أي من النطفة ونحوها { ويخرج الميت } أي من النطفة ونحوها مما لا ينمو

BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r4.claim: The final question about managing all affairs summarizes God’s comprehensive governance; the polytheists acknowledge that God alone does this.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r4.anchor: ومن يدبر الأمر } أي كله التدبير العام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r5.claim: Their admission that God alone provides and governs makes their failure to guard themselves from His punishment incoherent, since they associate partners in divinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r5.anchor: أي تجعلون وقاية بينكم وبين عقابه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r1.claim: Read each verse in its situation and context; language consists of utterances in settings, and wording appropriate in one setting may not fit another.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r1.anchor: لا ينبغي أن ينظر إلى الآيات مجردة، بل تؤخذ في مواطنها وسياقها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بين الزبير
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar adds that the preceding Yūnus questions about provision and control of hearing and sight have already awakened the audience, leaving only the reminder of punishment.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#6/r6.anchor: فحصل تحريكهم وتنبيههم بما لم يبق بعد إلا التذكير بعذابهم

BURHAN:v2p471/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p471/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p471/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī groups “who manages the affair” after “who provides for you” with the preceding category of coordinated expressions.
BURHAN:v2p471/r1.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري منه قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن يدبر الأمر ﴾ بعد قوله ﴿ قل من يرزقكم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p471/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p471/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p471/r2.claim: Coordinating synonyms or near-synonyms with واو adds emphasis; it occurs in clauses and especially in word pairs with different wording.
BURHAN:v2p471/r2.anchor: عطف أحد المترادفين على الآخر أو ما هو قريب منه في المعنى والقصد منه التأكيد وهذا إنما يجيء عند اختلاف اللفظ وإنما يحسن بالواو

ITQAN:v2p564/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p564/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p564/r3.claim: Hearing is singular because it is verbal-noun-like and its object, sound, is one kind; sight is plural because it names an organ whose objects—colors and forms—are diverse.
ITQAN:v2p564/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك إفراد السمع وجمع البصر لأن السمع غلب عليه المصدرية فأفرد بخلاف البصر فإنه اشتهر في الجارحة

ITQAN:v3p192#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p192#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p192#2/r1.claim: Conjoining a general category after a particular item broadens the statement, while naming the particular first emphasizes its importance; al-Suyuti rejects denial that this construction exists.
ITQAN:v3p192#2/r1.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم وجوده فأخطأ والفائدة فيه واضحة وهو التعميم وأفرد الأول بالذكر اهتماما بشأنه

ITQAN:v3p192#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p192#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p192#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats ومن يدبر الأمر after the questions about provision as an example of conjoining a general matter after a particular one.
ITQAN:v3p192#2/r2.anchor: وجعل منه الزمخشري ﴿ ومن يدبر الأمر ﴾ بعد قوله

NASHR:v2p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p223/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the yāʾ in all the listed forms of «الميتة/ميتا», «بلد ميت», and «الحي من الميت والميت من الحي».
NASHR:v2p223/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الياء في جميع ذلك، ووافقه نافع في يس الأرض الميتة

BURHAN:v1p130/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r7.claim: The wording contrasts nominal مخرج الميت in al-Anʿām with the verbal يخرج form in the second parallel passage.
BURHAN:v1p130/r7.anchor: فى الأنعام ﴿ يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ﴾ والثانى ﴿ يخرج ﴾ بالفعل

BURHAN:v4p7/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p7/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p7/r1.claim: Where context does not require plural, heaven is put in the singular to express the generic class.
BURHAN:v4p7/r1.anchor: ولما لم يكن في سورة يونس ما يقتضي ذلك أفردها إرادة للجنس

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.claim: An unnamed scholar proposes that repeating the relative and locative phrase specifies individuals; a single relative instead signals the general class and foregrounds the verse's main purpose, as in al-Raḥmān.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r15.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أنه تأمل ما في التنزيل العزيز من قوله تعالى: (من في السماوات والأرض) و: (من في السماوات ومن في الأرض)
